References and measured quantities

Inputs, acceptance,24 unit checks and numerical source were frozen before the first primary test/PDE execution. Checks cover analytic Mach3 normal-shock Rankine-Hugoniot identities, uniform parallel-channel flow, zero stationary-wall mass/energy flux, step-pressure force orientation, actual four-component budgets and raw failure retention. Newly executed separate C++17 MUSCL/generalized-minmod theta1.5/HLL/Heun references atNy80/160 are conservatively restricted for whole-fluid density/pressure L1 comparison. Ordinary public-ZIP verification reads saved reference data; reference source, contracts and execution records are bundled. The first referenceNy160 exhausted its preregistered120second budget; that actual timeout is preserved. A reference revision removed only unnecessary diagnostic-string allocation and was repinned before first primary execution; physical inputs,arithmetic,CFL and acceptance values did not change. All24 tests, three final-time runs and45 gates passed with-W error. Primary density L1=.14754/.12878/.10265, pressure L1=.19373/.16015/.12242 and last-pair density slope=.327. Reference80/160 increments=.02636/.03063, about.257/.250 of the finest primary differences. Maximum four-component relative boundary-budget residual=2.99e-13; all integrated wall mass/energy fluxes are zero. The three primary grids took about46seconds on the original Mac; revised reference80/160 took about8/65seconds.

Verification limits and failures

The reference is separately implemented but shares the HLL family and Heun; no external AMROC,LAVA or RKDG engine was executed. Finite-grid numerical data are neither an exact2D solution nor an error bound. Without special corner treatment, a numerical entropy layer may be advected downstream; no agreement with corrected originalPPM fine structures is claimed. Whole-fluid differences,Linf and fixed corner density/pressure/entropy diagnostics are retained. Slopes do not prove pure spatial order; thin slip lines,roll-up,general geometries and high-order convergence remain unverified. Normalized maximum density differences=.592/.670/.665 do not decrease. Corner minima of log(p/rho^gamma)=-.0784/-.1224/-.3510 change substantially. This absolute entropy variable includes an arbitrary additive constant; a more-negative value is not itself an error increase. Neither stable corner extrema nor pointwise pattern convergence is established.

Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification

The same 2D Euler isentropic-vortex family is evolved at background Mach numbers .1 and .01 on 16², 32² and 64² grids to T=.1. Both Roe variants use unlimited central primitive-variable MUSCL reconstruction and SSPRK(3,3); one preconditions numerical dissipation with a Miczek-type matrix. Physical time and acoustic CFL=.2 are retained.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Download and execute the supplement

Low-Mach isentropic vortex: preconditioned Roe flux verification

The same nonlinear 2D Euler vortex is evolved to T=0.1 on N=16/32/64 at background Mach 0.1/0.01, comparing ordinary Roe with Miczek spatial flux preconditioning. Twelve fixed runs retain velocity and dynamically scaled pressure errors, conserved budgets, acoustic steps and actual stage states.

Methods, equations, figures and references

Methods used

  • Roe
  • Low-Mach PDE preconditioning
  • MUSCL reconstruction
  • SSPRK(3,3)

Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.

Equations

This example’s formulation and conditions

Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope

Both finite-volume variants use the same unlimited centered primitive-MUSCL reconstruction, the physical Euler flux and SSPRK(3,3); only Roe dissipation is replaced by D=P^-1|PA|. At each Roe state use the total-speed Mach with mu=min(1,max(M_local,M_infinity)) and delta=1/mu-1, applying the primitive Miczek matrix through conserved-variable Jacobians. A degree-two characteristic polynomial applies the matrix absolute value; a separate dense eigendecomposition checks it. Physical time and sound speed are unchanged; acoustic CFL=0.2 remains. Reconstructed faces and all three stages check positive density and pressure, without limiters, floors, repair, hidden retries or pseudo-time iteration. A forward-Euler amplification counterexample prevents claiming SSP/TVD or general nonlinear stability from the integrator name.

  • Compressible Euler equations

    Unforced 2D ideal-gas Euler is advanced in the original conservative variables and physical time. Fixed inputs use gamma=1.4, a periodic 20×20 box and a consistently scaled isentropic vortex with Mach-dependent background pressure.

Problem figure

A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.

Periodic moving isentropic vortex

This problem’s code and validation status

Exact / reference solutions

References and checks for this execution

Reference and validation scope

The original 32 unit tests passed, but one of 143 first-order spatial gates failed: finest M_infinity=0.01 whole-domain dynamic pressure error 0.16537 exceeded the fixed 0.1 threshold. Original sources, contract, all twelve fields and the failed global pressure plot are retained. Revision 2 gives both fluxes the same unlimited centered primitive MUSCL and adds three checks for reconstruction, raw face failure and actual-RHS linearization against independent matrices. Inputs, physical time, CFL and acceptance bytes are unchanged; the revised 35-test/143-gate contract was frozen before revision execution. Checks cover Roe conserved jumps and physical-flux differences, dense-matrix dissipation, the three stages and raw invalid-stage retention. Each background Mach/flux has 17^2 constant-state Fourier modes and powers 1/10/100 in stated physical acoustic-energy variables. Pressure errors divide by rho_infinity*|U_infinity|^2 rather than the large p_infinity; velocity errors divide by analytic vortex perturbations. Initial R_h-q_t for the translating analytic field is retained as truncation error, not converged steady residual. Revision 2 passed all 35 tests, twelve runs and 143 gates with -W error, taking about 4.4 seconds on the original Mac. At finest M_infinity=0.01, relative velocity L1 was 0.07411 for Roe and 0.01847 for preconditioning; fixed-core pressure errors were 0.04871/0.0006325. Whole-domain pressure errors were instead 0.01194/0.01260, slightly worse with preconditioning; M_infinity=0.1 similarly gave 0.0006653/0.0006737. Maximum relative conserved-budget residual was 4.24e-14. Dynamic-scale Gauss8/16 maximum difference was 4.08e-11 and analytic Euler substitution residual 1.09e-16. Sampled SSPRK3 spectral radii and stated energy-scaled matrix powers had maximum 1. Forward Euler exceeded 1 for both MUSCL variants, reaching about 1.03560 for preconditioning at M_infinity=0.01.

  • Same-problem reference · Analytic reference

    Isentropic vortex: analytic Euler field for low-Mach comparisons

    Analytic field for the same translating isentropic-vortex family. Pressure and velocity are evaluated after Gauss integration of conserved variables; finite-periodic Gaussian tails and quadrature error remain explicit.

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Periodic [-10,10]^2, gamma=1.4, beta=3, background density 1 and velocity (1,0.5). Set p_infinity=|U_infinity|^2/(gamma M_infinity^2), retaining the same flow and vortex strengths. Background Mach is not maximum local Mach. A whole-plane translating isentropic vortex is evaluated with minimum-image coordinates and a separately qualified Gaussian seam. Conserved cell means use eight-point tensor Gauss quadrature, checked against order 16; they are not closed-form exact means or a generic exactly periodic nonlinear vortex.

Editorial clarification

The implementation preconditions the numerical-flux dissipation matrix D=P⁻¹|PA|. It does not implement steady pseudo-time or dual-time acceleration, or validate an explicit convective time step. The SSPRK(3,3) name alone does not supply strong-stability or nonlinear positivity guarantees; fixed runs and sampled constant-state Fourier modes have distinct scopes. At the finest M∞=.01 grid, velocity error and vortex kinetic-energy retention improve, but whole-domain dynamically normalized pressure L1 is about .01194 for ordinary Roe and .01260 for preconditioned Roe. Pressure error is not uniformly improved. The vorticity/velocity-perturbation illustration is a central crop; diagnostics distinguish the whole box from a fixed core.

Reconstructed faces and all three stages check positive density and pressure, without limiters, floors, repair, hidden retries or pseudo-time iteration. Verification limits and failures

This is a short T=0.1 fixed-input, few-grid test, not a full circulation or long-time preservation study. The Fourier check covers selected uniform states, wave numbers and powers; it is no proof for all modes, nonlinear variable states or general positivity. Actual integration retains the acoustic CFL and does not use the displayed convective diagnostic step. Steady convergence acceleration, dual time, shock/contact robustness, general meshes and all Mach numbers remain unverified. Finite periodic-box seams, Gauss quadrature and primitive variables evaluated from cell means remain distinct qualifications. Pressure Mach dependence and local errors are retained. Unlimited MUSCL is selected for these smooth inputs, not a limiter, TVD method or general positivity guarantee. The original box-wide pressure waves are shown in a separate full-domain failed-trial figure rather than hidden by the gallery core crop. Velocity/core improvements do not imply globally better pressure: finest whole-domain pressure L1 is slightly larger with preconditioning and grows when background Mach is reduced by ten. No Mach-independent pressure accuracy follows from these measurements. Perturbation kinetic energy is a diagnostic computed from conserved cell means, not exact conservation of continuous kinetic energy.

Primary sources and review scope

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.

  1. Fabian Miczek, Friedrich K. Röpke and Philipp V. F. Edelmann (2015). New numerical solver for flows at various Mach numbers [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1051/0004-6361/201425059

    Review scope / review_level: selected-author-version-full-text: Section8 Eq56; Section4 explicit-RK3 discussion; AppendixA variable transforms; Section6 smooth piecewise-linear reconstruction without a limiter

    Selected author-version equations and RK3 discussion were checked. This short isentropic-vortex application does not reproduce the paper’s Gresho or implicit-integration experiments. Section 6 also motivates unlimited piecewise-linear reconstruction for smooth tests; this is independent motivation for the revision.

  2. Wasilij Barsukow, Philipp V. F. Edelmann, Christian Klingenberg, Fabian Miczek and Friedrich K. Röpke (2017). A Numerical Scheme for the Compressible Low-Mach Number Regime of Ideal Fluid Dynamics [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1007/s10915-017-0372-4

    Review scope / review_level: selected-full-text: Section3 Eqs21,31,32; Section5 Eq83 and Fourier-mode stability discussion

    Checked the modified dissipation, primitive matrix and restrictive forward-Euler stability result. The present SSPRK33 Fourier/stage checks are separate fixed-input evidence, not a general nonlinear or SSP guarantee.

  3. Seth C. Spiegel, H. T. Huynh and James R. DeBonis (2015). A Survey of the Isentropic Euler Vortex Problem using High-Order Methods [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.2514/6.2015-2444

    Review scope / review_level: selected-primary-report: parameterized vortex definitions and Sections IV.B/IV.C boundary discussion

    Checked the generalized vortex and finite-periodic-boundary qualifications. The selected beta3, mean velocity(1,.5) and background Mach values are explicit adaptations, not NASA/FR execution or figure reuse.

  4. Sigal Gottlieb and Chi-Wang Shu (1998). Total Variation Diminishing Runge-Kutta Schemes [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1090/S0025-5718-98-00913-2

    Review scope / review_level: author-bibliography and indexed author-PDF excerpts; direct PDF fetch unavailable

    Bibliography and indexed author-PDF excerpts were checked. No direct full-PDF reading is claimed; coefficients are also cross-checked against the author review below.

  5. Sigal Gottlieb, Chi-Wang Shu and Eitan Tadmor (2001). Strong Stability-Preserving High-Order Time Discretization Methods [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1137/S003614450036757X

    Review scope / review_level: selected-full-author-PDF: Section4 Proposition4.1 Eq4.2 printedp100/PDFpage12; Section2.2 Lemma2.1 printedp92/PDFpage4

    Checked the three-stage updates and the forward-Euler hypothesis behind SSP. No general SSP/TVD/nonlinear stability guarantee is borrowed for this Miczek flux; the stated Fourier matrices and actual stage states are checked separately.

validation-guderley.html:
Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification

HLL plus Heun follows a Guderley shock into stationary zero-pressure upstream gas at gamma=1.4, r in [0,0.75], t=-1 to -0.85 on 128/256/512 shells. Initialize the similarity field with Rs(-1)=0.6 and compare the pre-collapse trajectory, conserved shell means and budgets with a semi-analytic reference. The figure is a 2D section display of 1D radial results.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Download and execute the supplement

Run inside atlas-guderley-2026-11-23-r3 from the ZIP. This command executes all 1 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

Guderley converging shock: lightweight spherical-radial verification

An inward spherical Guderley shock in cold stationary gas is evolved from t=-1 to -0.85 on 128/256/512 radial shells. HLL fluxes and Heun steps are checked against a similarity eigenvalue/field, shock trajectory and discrete conservation budgets.

First-order spherical finite volumes use face area4pi*r^2 and shell volume4pi*delta(r^3)/3. Shared HLL flux divergence plus the radial-momentum pressure source p_i*delta(A)/V is advanced by Heun at CFL0.4. The center is reflecting with zero face area; the outer similarity state is evaluated at both actual RK times. All three conserved budgets integrate the actual boundary flux and geometric source using the same Heun weights. There are no state floors, pressure repairs or hidden step retries.

    Guderley converging shock: eigenvalue and spherical semi-analytic reference

    The pre-collapse branch of the spherical Guderley similarity solution at gamma=1.4 with a cold uniform upstream state. Eigenvalue shooting, similarity-ODE integration and shock-split shell quadrature make it semi-analytic rather than closed-form exact cell means. Routine replay reuses lambda from the retained qualification, freshly integrating the similarity ODE and quadrature; recomputing the eigenvalue and original ExactPack probes is a separate explicit command. This is an adapter to pinned ExactPack, not an independently implemented similarity evaluator. Collapse at the origin, the reflected shock and general equations of state remain outside this example.

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Fix gamma=1.4, three-dimensional spherical symmetry on r in [0,0.75], Rs(-1)=0.6 and t in [-1,-0.85]. Ahead of the inward shock the inner gas is exactly rho0=1,u0=p0=0. The outer region already contains the shocked similarity field; the entire initial domain is not a uniform cold state. Initial conserved shell means use order16 Gauss integration split at the exact shock, checked against order32. Reference pressure is p(mean conserved state), not mean primitive pressure.

Verification limits and failures

This is a short one-dimensional spherical verification away from collapse t=0. The singular origin, reflected branch, cylindrical geometry, other gammas and nonspherical perturbation stability are untested. Two-dimensional pictures map saved spherical shell means onto a meridional plane; they are not Cartesian2D evolution. The semi-analytic field is a numerically evaluated ODE/quadrature reference, not a closed-form exact cell average. Zero pressure is allowed in the cold upstream; cancellation-band negative internal energy density down to an absolute64eps is recorded. Sound-speed square-root guards only within that band have separate counts/minimum raw pressure and do not repair the state. No general nonlinear positivity theorem is claimed. Shock-position error in cell units does not decrease monotonically:1.13/2.27/2.54. Absolute radius error is about0.00665 for the first two grids and0.00372 for the finest. Density Linf differences0.258/0.271/0.266 and pressure Linf0.492/0.494/0.466 are also not monotonically decreasing. L1 reduction is not evidence that the discontinuity is pointwise resolved or that the collapse region converges.

Euler double rarefaction: positivity at every stage

A one-dimensional MUSCL finite-volume Euler double rarefaction combines Lax–Friedrichs fluxes, SSPRK(3,3) and mean-preserving positive-state scaling at each stage. Check the admissible CFL, density/pressure in cell means and face states, and conservation budgets from actual shared boundary fluxes separately.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Euler double rarefaction: positivity at every stage

Evolve the existing strong double rarefaction on 128/256/512 cells, connecting mean-preserving positivity scaling to MUSCL, global LF fluxes and SSPRK(3,3). Log density, pressure and boundary budgets for every FE substep and SSP convex combination.

Methods, equations, figures and references

Methods used

  • Lax–Friedrichs
  • MUSCL reconstruction
  • Mean-preserving positive-state scaling
  • SSPRK(3,3)

Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.

Equations

This example’s formulation and conditions

Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope

Unlimited conservative central linear reconstruction is scaled toward its mean with one common theta per cell until both endpoint densities/pressures are positive. The two endpoint mean remains the original conserved mean. Shared LF FE updates are combined by SSPRK(3,3), reconstructing/limiting before every flux stage. Epsilon1e-13 is a reconstruction target, not an injected density/energy floor. No average repair or hidden time-step retries are used.

  • Compressible Euler equations

    Unforced one-dimensional ideal-gas Euler at gamma=1.4 evolves cell means of density, momentum and total energy using linear conservative MUSCL reconstruction and shared Lax–Friedrichs fluxes.

Problem figure

A saved validation figure for this execution example. Its conditions and acceptance scope are documented by this page’s checks.

Euler double rarefaction

This problem’s code and validation status

Exact / reference solutions

References and checks for this execution

Reference and validation scope

Freeze 27 unit tests and 73 gates over three grids before execution. Retain negative raw endpoint pressures, then separately measure limited endpoints, FE means, SSP convex means, theta and all three boundary-flux conservation budgets. Cross-check the closed symmetric fan against the prior independent logarithmic-pressure root evaluator; record errors/refinement against conserved Gauss8/16 cell means.

  • Related-model reference · Semi-analytic reference

    Euler / double rarefaction

    γ=1.4, states (1,-2,0.4)/(1,2,0.4), [0,1], x0=0.5 and t=0.15 match the saved preview. Physical inputs match, but the card’s point samples and the saved computation’s finite-volume cell averages/discrete grid are different representations.

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Fix gamma1.4, x in [0,1], discontinuity x0=.5, outer primitive states(1,-2,.4)/(1,2,.4) and T=.15. The low-density central state remains strictly positive; this is not a vacuum-generating case. Use fixed global LF splitting speed a4 and dt*a/dx<=.4; assert every actual endpoint satisfies |u|+c<=a and the sufficient dt*a/dx<=1/2 condition.

Editorial clarification

The same fixed physical input as the existing double rarefaction uses gamma=1.4, left/right (rho,u,p)=(1,-2,.4)/(1,2,.4), [0,1], x0=.5 and t=.15. Its middle state has small positive density/pressure, unlike separate vacuum-generating data. Stage scaling is connected to sufficient CFL and Lax–Friedrichs wave-speed conditions for this scoped example, without certifying existing WENO, DG, MHD or general equations of state.

Adopted numerical method

Unlimited conservative central linear reconstruction is scaled toward its mean with one common theta per cell until both endpoint densities/pressures are positive. The two endpoint mean remains the original conserved mean. Shared LF FE updates are combined by SSPRK(3,3), reconstructing/limiting before every flux stage. Epsilon1e-13 is a reconstruction target, not an injected density/energy floor. No average repair or hidden time-step retries are used.

References and measured quantities

Freeze 27 unit tests and 73 gates over three grids before execution. Retain negative raw endpoint pressures, then separately measure limited endpoints, FE means, SSP convex means, theta and all three boundary-flux conservation budgets. Cross-check the closed symmetric fan against the prior independent logarithmic-pressure root evaluator; record errors/refinement against conserved Gauss8/16 cell means.

Verification limits and failures

Evidence covers this one P1 FV update and fixed input, not general MUSCL/WENO/DG, characteristic reconstruction, reflecting walls, vacuum generation or multidimensional positivity. Unlimited central slopes have no TVD, maximum-principle or nonoscillation guarantee. Raw pressure is evaluated only where raw density is positive; nonpositive raw density has its own count. Reference pressure is p(mean conserved q), not mean pressure. Gallery plots are saved one-dimensional x-t fields, not two-dimensional flow. No ExactPack or separate PDE engine is executed.

Zalesak-type 2D rotation: conservation, bounds and shape error

A two-dimensional scalar conservation law transports a slotted disk in a prescribed rigid-rotation velocity. Compare donor-cell upwinding and minmod MUSCL with the same SSPRK(3,3), checking full-turn mass, bounds, shape error and dependence on grid placement and initial angle. The base refinements use64²,128² and256² cells, with separate placement and initial-angle diagnostics at64².

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Zalesak-type 2D rotation: conservation, bounds and shape error

Rotate a slotted disk through one full turn with an actual 2D finite-volume solver, comparing donor-cell and minmod MUSCL. Eight runs combine three grids with half-cell-center and 45-degree-start probes; measure conservation, bounds at every SSP stage, shape error and slot filling.

Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.

Equations

This example’s formulation and conditions

Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope

Use analytic divergence-free normal face averages and one shared upwind flux per interface. Both piecewise-constant donor-cell and mean-preserving directional-minmod MUSCL use SSPRK(3,3). The four face-midpoint mean equals the cell mean; individual outgoing-face Courant<=1/4 gives a convex FE update. Check the actual .20 bound at every stage. No transported-state clipping/floors or rejected/retried steps are used.

  • Two-dimensional rotational advection

    Two-dimensional conservative transport of q with prescribed a=-omega(y-yc), b=omega(x-xc), whose divergence is zero. Shared face velocities and numerical fluxes update scalar cell means.

Exact / reference solutions

References and checks for this execution

Reference and validation scope

Freeze26 unit checks and158 gates across eight fixed runs before execution. Retain min/max of every FE candidate/SSP convex mean, shared-flux mass budgets, reconstruction mean preservation and three-grid L1/Linf/relative-L2 errors. Independent circle/convex-polygon intersection means are qualified against SciPy vertical-slice quadrature, total area and first moments. Also check quarter/half/three-quarter-turn errors and centroids so a wrong direction or speed cannot hide behind a full-turn return.

  • Same-problem reference · Analytic reference

    Zalesak-type slotted disk: rigid rotation and geometric cell means

    Fix the disk and slot geometry and compare stored initial/returned cell means. Distinguish indicator point samples and a finer PDE calculation from this geometric reference.

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Fix the dimensionless unit square, rotation center(.5,.5), disk center(.5,.75), radius.15, slot width.05/top y=.85, angular speed1, T=2pi and64²/128²/256² cells. The body is1 and exterior/slot0. Periodic normal face velocities match; the exact compact support stays away from the boundary. The periodic extension has a tangential-velocity seam, and diffusive tails reaching its fixed-width boundary band are measured.

Editorial clarification

This is scalar transport in a prescribed divergence-free rotation, not Euler-fluid evolution. It uses a Zalesak-type slotted-disk shape test without claiming implementation of Zalesak’s FCT algorithm. Pointwise indicator values and geometric conserved cell means are distinguished; numerical tails near periodic boundaries are also measured. The initial32²/64²/128² series passed26 tests and156/158 gates, but its finest relative L1 was about1.11675 for donor-cell(limit1.0) and.6023 for MUSCL(limit.55), so it failed. Retain all original inputs,criteria,fields and failed decisions. A new pre-execution contract refines the base series to64²/128²/256² without changing acceptance thresholds, flux algorithms or the26 tests. Revision 2 passed all 26 tests and all 158 gates over eight runs; tests plus the fixed-input driver took about 19.58 seconds within one 120-second budget. At N=256 the relative L1 errors are about 0.932256 for donor-cell and 0.394271 for MUSCL (ratio about 0.423); the maximum absolute mass change over all runs is about 8.90e-15. Recorded stage bounds are 0 to 1, including initial states, but bounds alone do not establish accurate slot preservation. The inner empty-slot probe weights the piecewise-constant cell-mean field; it is not a point value of the continuum solution. Mixed reference cells create a projection baseline, so numerical mean, reference mean and their excess are stored separately. At N=256 the excesses are about 0.63465 and 0.36501 for donor-cell/MUSCL, showing substantial remaining diffusion. At N=64 the MUSCL slot excess can exceed donor-cell, so no uniform improvement across every metric and grid is claimed. The N=256 mass fractions in the fixed-width 0.05 boundary band are about 0.0178615/0.000243761 for donor-cell/MUSCL. The compact exact field vanishes there; these periodic-boundary tails remain visible in the diagnostics.

Adopted numerical method

Use analytic divergence-free normal face averages and one shared upwind flux per interface. Both piecewise-constant donor-cell and mean-preserving directional-minmod MUSCL use SSPRK(3,3). The four face-midpoint mean equals the cell mean; individual outgoing-face Courant<=1/4 gives a convex FE update. Check the actual .20 bound at every stage. No transported-state clipping/floors or rejected/retried steps are used.

References and measured quantities

Freeze26 unit checks and158 gates across eight fixed runs before execution. Retain min/max of every FE candidate/SSP convex mean, shared-flux mass budgets, reconstruction mean preservation and three-grid L1/Linf/relative-L2 errors. Independent circle/convex-polygon intersection means are qualified against SciPy vertical-slice quadrature, total area and first moments. Also check quarter/half/three-quarter-turn errors and centroids so a wrong direction or speed cannot hide behind a full-turn return.

Verification limits and failures

This is an isolated0–1 standard slotted body with periodic boundaries. It does not implement Zalesak FCT, reproduce the original paper’s grid/boundaries or the entire Firedrake bell/cone/background demonstration. The inner-slot diagnostic area-weights piecewise-constant means over a fixed rectangle. Coarse exact cell projection can already give a nonzero baseline, which is reported separately from excess numerical filling. Two center/orientation probes do not establish universal isotropy, perfect shape retention or a maximum principle for arbitrary flows. Tiny geometric-area roundoff handling is distinguished from the absence of transported-state clipping.

Primary sources and review scope

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.

    Review scope / review_level: publisher bibliography and abstract inspected; direct full-paper open returned403; original test geometry and boundary conditions not audited

    Publisher record and abstract checked. The full original test geometry/grid/boundaries were not audited. This example does not implement or reproduce Zalesak FCT.

  2. Firedrake developers (n.d.). DG advection equation with upwinding [accessed 2026-11-23]

    Review scope / review_level: official documentation equations and source lines46,63–92: disk(.5,.75),R.15,slot(.475,.525),y<.85,velocity(.5−y,x−.5),T2pi; SSP equations43–45 and135–143

    Inspected official geometry, velocity, period and SSP formulas. The demo includes a bell, cone, background1, DQ1 elements and inflow1. This is an explicit isolated0–1 slotted-disk FV/periodic variant. No Firedrake software was executed or copied.

    Review scope / review_level: author-hosted paper selected sections1–3 actually inspected: PDE/incompressibility, FV means, minmod definition, donor-cell flux; no full-paper or numerical-table reproduction

    Review scope / review_level: official versioned API: QUADPACK integration, break points, epsabs/epsrel, reported error; use is evidenced by qualification receipts

    Versioned official API checked for QUADPACK, break points, tolerances and reported error. Independently integrated vertical sections are compared with circle/polygon areas; execution is established by saved receipts.

validation-weno-critical.html:
WENO critical points and epsilon dependence

Compare critical-point reconstruction from cell means using WENO-JS/Z power-two weights and actual periodic scalar transport. Separate epsilon choices, analytic cell means versus point values, and spatial error versus time-step effects. For the selected first-critical polynomial, both tiny-epsilon JS and Z show local rates about5; Z has a smaller leading error.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

WENO-JS/Z: fixed critical-point and epsilon comparison

Download and execute the supplement

Run inside atlas-weno-critical-2026-11-23 from the ZIP. This command executes all 1 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

WENO-JS/Z: fixed critical-point and epsilon comparison

Compare WENO5 JS and Z power-two weights from the same cell means, then evolve actual periodic transport. Retain three regularity classes, three epsilon choices, fixed grids and separate halved-time-step diagnostics.

Reference and validation scope

Pre-run contract fixes72 local reconstructions,24 PDE runs and36 pytest checks. Qualify analytic means against independent Gauss12 quadrature; retain local errors/weights, transport L1/L2/Linf, mass, stage finiteness, intermediate times and shared-flux budgets. Six finest-grid half-dt differences must be at most10% of corresponding continuum errors.

  • Related-model reference · Analytic reference

    Advection / sine translation

    Same periodic sine-transport model at speed one. The library amplitude is 0.25 versus 0.2 in the common fixed input; DG/CIP representations and output times also differ.

  • Related-model reference · Analytic reference

    WENO critical points: polynomial cell means and analytic periodic transport

    An additional constant-speed periodic-transport reference. The cos+.1sin³ cell means and local critical polynomials differ from the historical single-sine/CIP display.

  • Same-problem reference · Analytic reference

    FR/DG periodic sine advection: analytic reference at mean0.4 andT=.25

    Dimensionless u_t+u_x=0 on[0,1), periodic boundary, initial0.4+sin(2pi x), analytic0.4+sin(2pi(x-t)). Constant positive speed1 and uniform affine intervals.

Assumptions, units and boundaries

Local polynomials have center x=0 and target h/2, h=1/64…1/512. Transport uses periodic[0,1], unit speed, q₀=cos(2πx)+.1sin³(2πx), T=1 and32/64/128 cells. All evolved states/references are FV cell means, not point samples.

Editorial clarification

Order gates concern the chosen first-critical interface reconstruction; second-critical values remain diagnostic. Fixed epsilon depends on amplitude/units. Distinguish reconstruction order from PDE convergence and this FV implementation from original FD papers. No shock/Euler/MHD, arbitrary higher-critical-point, universal stability/TVD or positivity guarantee is claimed. For the selected first-critical polynomial, BOTH tiny-epsilon JS and Z have local reconstruction rates of about5 on the last grid pair. JS absolute error decreases from about9.77e-9 to2.88e-13 and Z from about2.12e-9 to5.70e-14, with a finest Z/JS ratio about.198. This fixed example demonstrates a smaller leading error; it does not observe JS order loss or establish universal critical-point order recovery by Z. The second-critical class remains a separate diagnostic.

Primary sources and review scope

Bibliography, abstracts, selected original sections and executed official code have distinct review scopes. Full papers and third-party code are not reproduced wholesale, and no blanket full-text audit is claimed.

  1. Guang-Shan Jiang and Chi-Wang Shu (1996). Efficient Implementation of Weighted ENO Schemes [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1006/jcph.1996.0130

    Review scope / review_level: NASA-hosted ICASE95-73 preprint selected sections1–3: candidate Table1, optimal Table2, equations2.15–2.16 and3.1–3.9; text layer inspected, not full paper/numerical tables

    Inspected selected sections1–3 of the NASA preprint for candidates, weights, indicators and finite-difference point-value conventions. Original experiments/Euler characteristic reconstruction are not reproduced.

  2. Rafael Borges, Monique Carmona, Bruno Costa and Wai Sun Don (2008). An improved weighted essentially non-oscillatory scheme for hyperbolic conservation laws [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1016/j.jcp.2007.11.038

    Review scope / review_level: Author-institution publication record and abstract inspected; publisher full text returned403; original full paper and numerical experiments not audited

    Inspected the author institution bibliography/abstract. Full publisher text was unavailable; no full-paper audit or replication of original power-one experiments is claimed. The implemented power-two formula was checked in another primary research paper.

  3. Bart S. van Lith, Jan H. M. ten Thije Boonkkamp and Wilbert L. IJzerman (2017). Embedded WENO: A design strategy to improve existing WENO schemes [accessed 2026-11-23] · DOI: 10.1016/j.jcp.2016.11.026

    Review scope / review_level: Institution-hosted accepted manuscript section2 equations2–15 (PDF pages4–8) and selected section4.2 (PDF page22) text inspected; screenshot requests cache-missed; not a full-paper review

    Inspected cell-average equations2–3, candidate/linear weights4–7, JS indicators/weights8–13, Z weights15 and selected power-two discussion in section4.2. The paper’s new embedded schemes are not implemented and its PDF is not redistributed.

validation-shallow-water.html:
Shallow water: topography, lakes and dry beds

Check shallow-water bed sources and hydrostatic reconstruction with wet/emerged lakes and a SWASHES steady Bernoulli flow. A separate flat-bed Ritter dam break tests genuinely dry states, conservation budgets and a fixed-depth front.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Additional validation indexCode and tests / ZIPIndependent-extraction receipt
SWASHES topographic flow: lakes and nonzero steady dischargeDry-bed dam break: actual wetting and dry states

Download and execute the supplement

Run inside atlas-shallow-water-2026-11-23 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

SWASHES topographic flow: lakes and nonzero steady discharge

Check two lake equilibria separately from nonzero subcritical flow, distinguishing lake preservation from moving-flow discretization error.

Methods, equations, figures and references

Methods used

  • Godunov-type finite volumes
  • HLL
  • Forward Euler

Methods used by this fixed-input execution. Their guides describe applicable conditions and the checked scope.

Equations

This example’s formulation and conditions

Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope

Hydrostatic reconstruction, shared HLL flux and left/right pressure corrections discretize the bed source; forward Euler and face CFL .4. Lakes use reflecting walls. Moving subcritical boundaries impose upstream q and downstream h, extrapolating the other datum. No state floors, clipping or retries. Algebraically factor HLL updates into nonnegative water packets; advected momentum uses those same rounded masses, without a small-depth threshold or subsequent repair.

  • Shallow-water equations with bed source

    1D, g=9.81, L=25m, compact parabolic bed z=.2-.05(x-10)^2 on8<x<12. Lakes at surface .5/.1m use200 cells. Moving flow q=4.42m2/s, downstream h=2m uses100/200/400 cells to2s. Initialize the steady branch, not the published rest-to-steady transient.

1D, g=9.81, L=25m, compact parabolic bed z=.2-.05(x-10)^2 on8<x<12. Lakes at surface .5/.1m use200 cells. Moving flow q=4.42m2/s, downstream h=2m uses100/200/400 cells to2s. Initialize the steady branch, not the published rest-to-steady transient.

Editorial clarification

Exact lake balance concerns the represented cell bed. Moving steady states retain finite-time numerical error. Transcritical flows, jumps, friction, rain, infiltration, 2D flow and fully discrete entropy stability are outside scope. The final revision passed31 unit checks and all109 gates over8 group runs. The finest moving steady case,N400, has depthL1 about.0249108 and relative depthL1 about.000505933. Represented-bed lake balance, finite-time moving steady errors and dry-bed front errors are retained separately.

Adopted numerical method

Hydrostatic reconstruction, shared HLL flux and left/right pressure corrections discretize the bed source; forward Euler and face CFL .4. Lakes use reflecting walls. Moving subcritical boundaries impose upstream q and downstream h, extrapolating the other datum. No state floors, clipping or retries. Algebraically factor HLL updates into nonnegative water packets; advected momentum uses those same rounded masses, without a small-depth threshold or subsequent repair.

Nonperiodic walls: cavity and manufactured flow

Solve a Re100 lid-driven cavity and manufactured flow with a nonperiodic wall-bounded2D vorticity/streamfunction method. Compare original finite-grid Ghia tables, wall shear and grid refinement, keeping a separate pressure-Poisson/gradient manufactured problem distinct.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

level-set.html:
Level sets: moving interfaces and comparison with VOF

A level set embeds a curve or surface as the zero contour of a grid function and evolves that function. It connects transport, Hamilton–Jacobi equations and interface geometry, with a representation that naturally accommodates merging and splitting. Start with the equations, then inspect small reproducible two-dimensional circle motions.

Represent the interface by phi=0

Γ(t)={x:ϕ(x,t)=0},ϕ<0  inside,ϕ>0  outside\Gamma(t)=\{\mathbf{x}:\phi(\mathbf{x},t)=0\},\qquad\phi<0\; ext{inside},\quad\phi>0\; ext{outside}Γ(t)={x:ϕ(x,t)=0},ϕ<0inside,ϕ>0outside

Here the interior is negative and the exterior positive. Function values are neither fluid density nor volume fraction. A monotone transformation retaining the zero set leaves the interface unchanged while changing gradients and numerical behavior. Some sources reverse the sign; normals and normal speeds must use the same convention.

An interface transported by a velocity

DϕDt=0⟹ϕt+u⋅∇ϕ=0 rac{D\phi}{Dt}=0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\phi_t+\mathbf{u}\cdot abla\phi=0DtDϕ​=0⟹ϕt​+u⋅∇ϕ=0

Differentiate the condition that phi is constant along a trajectory moving with velocity u to obtain the transport equation. Prescribed-velocity interface transport differs from solving coupled two-phase velocities and pressure. Upwind differences, ENO/WENO and time integration discretize this equation; they are choices in addition to the interface representation.

Normals, curvature and normal motion

With a negative interior the normal points outward; the two-dimensional circle has kappa=1/r in this convention. A prescribed normal speed gives a Hamilton–Jacobi equation. A signed distance has unit gradient where differentiable; circle centers and points with nonunique nearest interfaces need not be smooth. Diagnostics therefore focus on a band near the interface; curvature-driven motion is explained but not executed here.

What redistancing repairs and can change

General advection need not retain a distance function. An auxiliary pseudo-time tau equation can restore distance quality without advancing physical time t. Preserving an ideal zero set does not guarantee an interpolated discrete interface stays fixed. The example uses first-order Godunov iterations with sign frozen per call; it is not the constrained higher-order Sussman–Fatemi scheme, and no position or area improvement is assumed.

Comparison of formulations, conservation and implementation scope
AspectLevel setVOF
Stored quantitySigned function phi; interface phi=0Cell fluid-volume fraction F
GeometryNormals/curvature from derivatives of phiInterface reconstruction and geometry from fractions
ConservationOrdinary transport/redistancing does not guarantee enclosed volumeConservative shared face fluxes provide a volume balance

For a prescribed incompressible velocity, volume fractions admit conservative transport. Cancellation of shared interior face fluxes gives a global balance with boundary fluxes. Bounds0<=F<=1 additionally depend on fluxes, reconstruction and CFL conditions; conservation alone is insufficient. Conserving phi itself does not conserve its enclosed area. The area diagnosed from piecewise-linear phi here is not a conservatively advected VOF fraction.

Small 2D examples: translation and off-center rotation

Radius.15 on the unit square, T=1. Translation starts at(.3,.35) with velocity(.2,.1). Rotation carries a circle centered at(.68,.5) once about(.5,.5), at angular speed2pi. ENO2 one-sided differences and Heun RK2 use32²/64²/128² grids and Courant number<=.35. Analytic ghost values are prescribed at every stage while all interior values are numerically updated. These are prescribed boundaries, not periodic conditions.

Both cases compare advection alone against five redistancing pseudo-steps every.1 physical time. Observe0/.25/.5/.75/1; the rotation checks intermediate displacement as well as full-turn return.

What the error measurements mean

Z_h contains linearly interpolated grid-edge zero crossings; E_Gamma is the maximum radial error at these samples, not a continuous-interface Hausdorff distance. Geometric area clips linear phi on triangles and compares against pi*r², retaining initial geometric bias. Coupled grid/time refinement of advection alone observes about1.90 for translation and2.02 for rotation. SeparateN64 CFL-halving sensitivity is recorded; this is not a proof of pure spatial order.

Finest-grid worst relative area error changes about0.22% to0.93% for translation and1.06% to2.02% for rotation, from advection alone to redistancing. The simple redistancing increases error in these fixed runs. Distance-gradient quality, zero-interface accuracy and enclosed-volume balance are distinct diagnostics.

Scope and related reading

This release transports circles in prescribed velocities. It does not validate topology changes, curvature flow, surface tension or two-phase flow, nor benchmark VOF performance. Downloads retain analytic reference formulas, full2D final fields, intermediate interface samples, CSV, input hashes, all decisions and each redistancing area change. The existing Zalesak slotted-disk material is a separate conservative scalar-transport example; its code is not relabeled as a VOF implementation.

Primary publications, supporting sources and review scope

Distinguish original research, later variants, author monographs, pedagogical articles and official references. Bibliographic verification differs from consulting selected passages; neither implies a full-paper audit or numerical reproduction. Access-depth notes accompany each source.

Assumptions, units and boundaries

All quantities are nondimensional on[0,1]², with phi<0 inside. The prescribed divergence-free rigid motion keeps the circle away from the boundary. Two exterior ghost layers receive analytic data at each RK stage; this is not a periodic boundary. Every interior value is numerically advanced. Observe0/.25/.5/.75/1; max(|u|+|v|)dt/dx<=.35.

Analytic center motion and signed distance provide the reference. Take worst errors over the four positive common observation times. Verification limits and failures

Sampled radial error is not a Hausdorff distance. Observed order refines dx and dt together rather than isolating spatial order. Redistancing need not improve area or position; errors increase here even on the finest grid. No numerical VOF ranking, separate PDE engine, topology change, curvature flow, surface tension or two-phase Navier–Stokes validation is claimed. The two motions are conditions of one transported-circle-interface problem.

spectral-element.title: Spectral elements: high-order finite elements and 2D Poisson
spectral-element.html:
Spectral elements: high-order finite elements and 2D Poisson

The spectral element method (SEM) partitions a domain into elements and approximates the field with high-degree local polynomials. It connects finite-element assembly with high-order approximation of smooth functions. This chapter adopts a continuous Galerkin Legendre GLL variant and a small reproducible two-dimensional Poisson problem.

Connect high-order local polynomials

uh∣Ke(ξ,η)=∑i,j=0pUijeℓi(ξ)ℓj(η),uh∈C0(Ω)u_h|_{K_e}(\xi,\eta)=\sum_{i,j=0}^{p}U^e_{ij}\ell_i(\xi)\ell_j(\eta),\qquad u_h\in C^0(\Omega)uh​∣Ke​​(ξ,η)=i,j=0∑p​Uije​ℓi​(ξ)ℓj​(η),uh​∈C0(Ω)

Map each square to reference coordinates in [−1,1]². Shared boundary degrees of freedom assemble a C0 field, without imposing continuous derivatives. SEM belongs to the high-order finite-element family; finite elements in general are not restricted to linear elements. Element-local polynomials also differ from a single global Fourier expansion.

Start from the Poisson weak form

∫Ω∇vh⋅∇uh dΩ=∫Ωvhf dΩ,vh∣∂Ω=0\int_\Omega\nabla v_h\cdot\nabla u_h\,d\Omega=\int_\Omega v_h f\,d\Omega,\qquad v_h|_{\partial\Omega}=0∫Ω​∇vh​⋅∇uh​dΩ=∫Ω​vh​fdΩ,vh​∣∂Ω​=0

Multiply −Laplacian u=f by a test function and integrate by parts, transferring one derivative to each factor. Zero Dirichlet tests remove the boundary term. This implementation approximates the integrals with GLL quadrature for constant coefficients and affine squares.

GLL nodes, quadrature and matrices

(1−ξi2)Pp′(ξi)=0,wi=2p(p+1)Pp(ξi)2,i=0,…,p(1-\xi_i^2)P_p^\prime(\xi_i)=0,\qquad w_i=\frac{2}{p(p+1)P_p(\xi_i)^2},\qquad i=0,\ldots,p(1−ξi2​)Pp′​(ξi​)=0,wi​=p(p+1)Pp​(ξi​)22​,i=0,…,p
Dij=ℓj′(ξi),W=diag⁡(wi),S=DTWD,Ke=hyhxS⊗W+hxhyW⊗SD_{ij}=\ell_j^\prime(\xi_i),\quad W=\operatorname{diag}(w_i),\quad S=D^TWD,\quad K_e=\frac{h_y}{h_x}S\otimes W+\frac{h_x}{h_y}W\otimes SDij​=ℓj′​(ξi​),W=diag(wi​),S=DTWD,Ke​=hx​hy​​S⊗W+hy​hx​​W⊗S
bije=hxhy4wiwjf(xe,i,ye,j),KU=bb^e_{ij}=\frac{h_xh_y}{4}w_iw_jf(x_{e,i},y_{e,j}),\qquad KU=bbije​=4hx​hy​​wi​wj​f(xe,i​,ye,j​),KU=b

The p+1 GLL nodes are the roots of the derivative of the degree-p Legendre polynomial plus both endpoints. The one-dimensional quadrature is exact through degree 2p−1. Nodal interpolation makes the quadrature mass diagonal, not exactly integrated for every degree-2p product. Two-dimensional stiffness also contains transverse products, so the quadrature convention matters. Assemble local tensor-product stiffness/load contributions, eliminate the boundary values and solve the sparse system.

Comparison with the existing P1 finite elements

Small example:2D Poisson h/p refinement

Ω=(0,1)2,u∗=sin⁡(πx)sin⁡(πy),f=2π2u∗,u∣∂Ω=0\Omega=(0,1)^2,\quad u_*=\sin(\pi x)\sin(\pi y),\quad f=2\pi^2u_*,\quad u|_{\partial\Omega}=0Ω=(0,1)2,u∗​=sin(πx)sin(πy),f=2π2u∗​,u∣∂Ω​=0

At p=2, use 2/4/8 SEM elements per coordinate and 4/8/16 subdivisions for the existing triangular P1 FEM. Both have 9/49/225 free unknowns. Separately fix 2 x 2 elements and vary p=1..6. The comparison executes byte-identical modules from the published Numart distribution; that historical release remains unchanged.

Distinguish residual, continuous error and observed order

EL2=[∫Ω(uh−u∗)2 dΩ]1/2,EH1=[∫Ω∣∇uh−∇u∗∣2 dΩ]1/2E_{L^2}=\left[\int_\Omega(u_h-u_*)^2\,d\Omega\right]^{1/2},\quad E_{H^1}=\left[\int_\Omega|\nabla u_h-\nabla u_*|^2\,d\Omega\right]^{1/2}EL2​=[∫Ω​(uh​−u∗​)2dΩ]1/2,EH1​=[∫Ω​∣∇uh​−∇u∗​∣2dΩ]1/2
EL2∼hp+1,EH1∼hp(smooth solution and resolved quadrature)E_{L^2}\sim h^{p+1},\qquad E_{H^1}\sim h^p\quad\text{(smooth solution and resolved quadrature)}EL2​∼hp+1,EH1​∼hp(smooth solution and resolved quadrature)

Integrate errors at separate higher-order Gauss points, not only at GLL nodes. A small linear-system residual alone does not imply a small continuous-PDE error. On the last h refinement, p2 SEM gives L2 order about 3.04 and H1-seminorm order 2.01; P1 FEM gives 1.97 and 0.99. At 225 free unknowns, L2 errors are about 2.49e−4 for SEM and 5.38e−3 for P1. At p6 on 2 x 2 elements, L2 error is about 3.78e−7.

These observations depend on smoothness, boundaries, element geometry, quadrature and solver choices. They establish neither universal p convergence near singularities nor a speed/accuracy ranking for all problems. Curved elements, mixed velocity/pressure spaces and fluid coupling are outside this execution.

Related implementations: Nek5000 and nekRS

Nek5000 is a high-order spectral-element flow solver. nekRS is the related CPU/GPU successor described by the official project. Follow those links for their documentation and source. The small Python Poisson code does not execute or validate either flow solver or its performance. Patera’s original paper supplies historical bibliographic context; the implemented Legendre GLL variant is separately specified.

flux-reconstruction.title: Flux reconstruction: flux correction, DG and 1D periodic advection
flux-reconstruction.html:
Flux reconstruction: flux correction, DG and 1D periodic advection

Flux reconstruction (FR) builds high-order conservation-law discretizations by correcting a polynomial flux inside each element with shared interface fluxes. Elements exchange information through numerical fluxes rather than enforcing a continuous solution. The correction function is part of the method definition; the name FR alone specifies neither accuracy nor stability.

Separate solution points from numerical interface fluxes

ut+aux=0,x∈[0,1),u(x+1,t)=u(x,t),u∗(x,t)=0.4+sin⁡(2π(x−at))u_t+a u_x=0,\quad x\in[0,1),\quad u(x+1,t)=u(x,t),\quad u_*(x,t)=0.4+\sin(2\pi(x-at))ut​+aux​=0,x∈[0,1),u(x+1,t)=u(x,t),u∗​(x,t)=0.4+sin(2π(x−at))
uh(ξ)=∑j=0pujℓj(ξ),fD(ξ)=∑j=0pf(uj)ℓj(ξ)u_h(\xi)=\sum_{j=0}^{p}u_j\ell_j(\xi),\qquad f^D(\xi)=\sum_{j=0}^{p}f(u_j)\ell_j(\xi)uh​(ξ)=j=0∑p​uj​ℓj​(ξ),fD(ξ)=j=0∑p​f(uj​)ℓj​(ξ)

Map each interval to ξ in [−1,1] and store values at p+1 solution points. Extrapolation to a face gives two traces from neighboring elements. For this constant-speed problem choose the left state when a>0 and the right state when a<0, giving one shared upwind flux per face.

Connect face fluxes with correction functions

fC(ξ)=fD(ξ)+(fL∗−fLD)gL(ξ)+(fR∗−fRD)gR(ξ)f^C(\xi)=f^D(\xi)+(f_L^*-f_L^D)g_L(\xi)+(f_R^*-f_R^D)g_R(\xi)fC(ξ)=fD(ξ)+(fL∗​−fLD​)gL​(ξ)+(fR∗​−fRD​)gR​(ξ)
gL(−1)=1, gL(1)=0,gR(−1)=0, gR(1)=1,u˙i=−2h∂ξfC(ξi)g_L(-1)=1,\ g_L(1)=0,\qquad g_R(-1)=0,\ g_R(1)=1,\qquad\dot u_i=-\frac{2}{h}\partial_\xi f^C(\xi_i)gL​(−1)=1, gL​(1)=0,gR​(−1)=0, gR​(1)=1,u˙i​=−h2​∂ξ​fC(ξi​)

Here fD is the element-local flux polynomial and f* is the shared numerical flux. Distribute their face differences using gL/gR so that the corrected flux matches f* at the endpoints. Differentiate it at the solution points to evolve the state. Distinguish these unknowns and flux corrections from the different reconstruction procedures in MUSCL/WENO.

A Radau choice that recovers DG

gL=(−1)p2(Pp−Pp+1),gR=12(Pp+Pp+1)g_L=\frac{(-1)^p}{2}(P_p-P_{p+1}),\qquad g_R=\frac12(P_p+P_{p+1})gL​=2(−1)p​(Pp​−Pp+1​),gR​=21​(Pp​+Pp+1​)
Mu˙=2h[aDTMu−tRfR∗+tLfL∗],M=diag⁡(wi)M\dot{\mathbf u}=\frac{2}{h}\left[aD^TM\mathbf u-\mathbf t_R f_R^*+\mathbf t_L f_L^*\right],\qquad M=\operatorname{diag}(w_i)Mu˙=h2​[aDTMu−tR​fR∗​+tL​fL∗​],M=diag(wi​)

Use Gauss solution points and the displayed Radau corrections. M is the diagonal Gauss-weight matrix, tL/tR extrapolate to faces and D differentiates on the reference interval. For a constant linear flux on affine intervals, this FR formulation corresponds to nodal DG. Modal Legendre coefficients represent the same polynomial when initial projection, flux and time stepping match. Nonlinear flux aliasing, other quadratures and other corrections require separate conditions.

Comparison with the existing modal DG

Small example: translate a sine by a quarter period

Initial 0.4+sin(2pi x), speed 1, T=.25; execute p=1/2 on 8/16/32 cells. Bundle byte-identical published DG modules and run each configuration. During h refinement enforce scaled Courant(2p+1)|a|dt/h<=.15. The final wave has actually moved; the calculation does not use a stationary initial picture as evidence of transport.

Separate conservation, dissipation and time error

Ih=∑eh2∑iwiue,i,dIhdt=0,ddt12∥uh∥L22=−∣a∣2∑faces[uh]2I_h=\sum_e\frac{h}{2}\sum_iw_iu_{e,i},\quad \frac{dI_h}{dt}=0,\qquad \frac{d}{dt}\frac12\|u_h\|_{L^2}^2=-\frac{|a|}{2}\sum_{\rm faces}[u_h]^2Ih​=e∑​2h​i∑​wi​ue,i​,dtdIh​​=0,dtd​21​∥uh​∥L22​=−2∣a∣​faces∑​[uh​]2

Shared face fluxes cancel in the periodic mass balance. The semidiscrete quadratic energy dissipates with interface jumps under upwinding. This does not guarantee stability at arbitrary timesteps or nonlinear entropy stability. Also measure every RK stage’s mass and each completed step’s energy.

U˙=AhU,Uexp⁡(T)=exp⁡(TAh)U(0),Et=∥URK3(T)−Uexp⁡(T)∥M\dot U=A_hU,\quad U_{\exp}(T)=\exp(TA_h)U(0),\quad E_t=\|U_{\rm RK3}(T)-U_{\exp}(T)\|_MU˙=Ah​U,Uexp​(T)=exp(TAh​)U(0),Et​=∥URK3​(T)−Uexp​(T)∥M​

Continuous L2 errors use additional Gauss points. Coupled h/dt observed orders are about 1.99 at p1 and 3.00 at p2. The maximum FR/published-DG difference is about 4.0e−15; maximum stage mass change is about 3.6e−15.

Compute an exponential action of the same spatial matrix as a separate time propagator. At p2/N32, RK3 time error is about 9.44e−9 and halves in timestep to 1.18e−9, a ratio about.125. This is not an independent spatial PDE solver. Preserve the initial dense-exponential warning and subsequent JSON scalar-type failure with their original source/input/results; fixes retain every numerical acceptance threshold.

Related implementation: PyFR and scope

PyFR is FR-based flow software supporting unstructured meshes and CPU/GPU execution. Follow its official overview and source. This small Python example neither installs nor runs or benchmarks PyFR. Nonlinear fluxes, shocks, limiters, general correction families, curved meshes and multidimensional FR require separate verification.

validation-instability-growth.html:
KH/RT initial growth and independent linear references

Compare actual small-amplitude nonlinear2D runs with separately derived continuous Fourier–Galerkin linear IVPs. Separate finite-time growth, spatial, temporal and amplitude effects.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Additional validation indexCode and tests / ZIPIndependent-extraction receipt
KH initial growth in a smooth periodic shear layerRT initial growth in smooth Boussinesq double layers

Download and execute the supplement

Run inside atlas-instability-growth-2026-11-23-r2 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

validation-mhd-transport.html:
Independent MHD transport, waves and compression comparisons

Evolve all8conserved components with HLLD/MUSCL/Heun and2D CT. Compare wave means or unmodified Athena++ loop/late-OT fields, separating independent reference spatial/time increments.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Download and execute the supplement

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt

validation-moving-waves.html:
Nonuniform ALE transport and2D rotating shallow-water waves

Time-advance conservative ALE transport on genuinely nonuniform moving cells with GCL, and2D linear rotating C-grid shallow-water waves. A prescribed-ALE Saltzman-type piston and limited sphere transport/axisymmetric balance are separate additions; general global Williamson dynamics remain unverified.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Download and execute the supplement

Run inside atlas-moving-waves-2026-11-23 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

validation-relativistic.html:
SRHD collision and nonlinear SRMHD Alfven wave

Compare an SRHD head-on collision with a Taub two-shock solution and full7-state finite-amplitude SRMHD wave with independent tensor formulas/conserved means. Space is1D; x–t pictures are not2D flow.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Warm PIC: Landau damping and two-stream instability

Compare self-consistent weighted full-f PIC with independently formulated dielectric dispersion and linear Volterra IVPs.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. validation-dsmc-wall.html:
Finite-Knudsen Couette and Fourier flows

Compare physical-time hard-sphere collisions,flux-weighted wall reemission and budgets with independent SPARTA references.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

This example’s formulation and conditions

Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope

Disjoint cell-local random pairs with even/odd finite-N physical-time sigma*g acceptance,energy-based safe majorant and predeclared bounded subcycling; no probability caps. Exact flight-to-wall and flux-conditioned diffuse/reservoir velocities with remaining flight time. Open-reservoir macro counts use unbiased floor(mean)+Bernoulli(fraction) per face/species/half-stream to reduce artificial sampling variance; no Poisson number-fluctuation or thermodynamic-fluctuation reproduction claim. Retain the original four seeds and append the next eight consecutive seeds; uniform permutation/stable integer sorting preserves the ideal within-cell matching law,not RNG consumption or bit-identical trajectories. Edition2026-11-24 only reuses immutable reservoir coefficients and an inverse-CDF residual at unchanged v,fuses concatenation in unchanged keep-left-right order,and reversibly narrows range-checked integer sort keys to uint8 before the same stable sort. Original permutation/RNG calls,equal-key particle order,collision pairs and scientific inputs remain unchanged. The first three changes passed163component checks; a separate348check study qualifies the sort-key composition with exact byte/RNG comparisons. Importance sampling and correlated-Gaussian diagnostics

Study importance-weighted tails and 2D correlated-Gaussian MCMC, separating analytic targets, same-data diagnostic comparisons and fresh-sample checks.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Download and execute the supplement

Run inside atlas-stochastic-estimation-2026-11-24 from the ZIP. This command executes all 2 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

validation-reverse-higher-ad.html:
Reverse mode, HVPs and nonsmooth branches

Independent hand-derived references check a small original tape, separating fixed-state partials, implicit total derivatives and executed branches.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Additional validation indexCode and tests / ZIPIndependent-extraction receipt
Original reverse-mode VJP and JVP/VJP dualityHessian-vector products and fixed-state versus implicit derivativesDerivative scope at kinks, branches and stopping decisions

Download and execute the supplement

Run inside atlas-reverse-higher-ad-2026-11-24 from the ZIP. This command executes all 3 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

Adjoints through time steps, folds and distributed coefficients

Compare tangents and adjoints of discrete maps, separating reference accuracy, requested residuals, owned buffers and recomputation.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

validation-inverse-optimization.html:
Optimization, noise and regularization in the Bratu inverse problem

Retain existing synthetic observations and compare GN/LM, quasi-Newton methods and regularization selection on small fixed controls.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Bratu comparisons of GN, LM and bounded least squaresBFGS and three-pair L-BFGS at known minimaNoise, model discrepancy and finite gamma paths

Download and execute the supplement

Run inside atlas-inverse-optimization-2026-11-24 from the ZIP. This command executes all 3 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

validation-ode-adaptivity.html:
Stiff ODEs, RK45 and boundary splitting

Small fixed inputs validate Robertson and van der Pol, RK45 interpolation/events, and splitting with inhomogeneous boundaries. Independent references distinguish local estimates from actual errors and temporal from spatial errors.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

validation-steady-rk.html:
Modal damping of steady multistage RK

A 16-component periodic linear field measures pseudo-time residual damping with stable, neutral and expanding controls. This is distinct from fourth-order accuracy for nonlinear physical-time problems.

These additional validation supplements are managed separately from the common 22-example registry. Receipts cover independent ZIP extraction, tests and every fixed input within each group. Changes of settings, methods or step sizes do not add independent physical problems.

Routine supplement CI runs the supplement groups listed in the public registry with NumPy,SciPy and pytest. It checks versions,inputs and execution records for stored independent references and distinguishes their reuse from new reference computations. The existing common22-case suite,including quantum convergence,remains manual on explicit need; released artifacts,criteria and history are preserved.

Real-space mode damping with steady multistage RK

Download and execute the supplement

Run inside atlas-steady-rk-2026-11-24 from the ZIP. This command executes all 1 fixed cases in the supplement. The bundled results/ contains stored outputs. Rerun into a new output/ directory, and choose another fresh directory for subsequent runs.

python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
python -m pytest -q
python run.py --input inputs.json --output output

Matplotlib is optional for redrawing saved figures; ordinary scientific execution does not require it.

Real-space mode damping with steady multistage RK

Apply four steady residual stages on a periodic grid, separating damping, neutrality and amplification of discrete modes. The retained first run missed the original absolute residual goal in the expanding control.

Formulation, approximation and diagnostic scope

Original scalar Newton position constraints, RATTLE final tangent impulses and SHAKE position pairs. SHAKE momentum is centered only at interior nodes; endpoint momenta are absent. SHAKE solves columns are eta, eta/h^2, position residual and Newton updates. Column1 uses the uniform recurrence normalization eta/h^2. For the first constrained half-step startup, the physical multiplier is 2*eta/h^2; later full position-Verlet steps use eta/h^2. Reverse-pair steps all use the later recurrence convention. RATTLE has its separate five-column normalization. No scientific gate or plot uses SHAKE column1.
